input.title: A: Scaffold Alltag Vite+React+TS+Tailwind app with shared contracts, gate and stubs
input.spec:
Scaffold the Alltag app (read .orchestrator/idea.md sections 3, 4, 6 and .orchestrator/human-direction-2026-10-10.md "Hard constraints" first). Write every file by hand; never run a generator that prompts. All later tasks consume the contracts you define here and add NO dependencies, so install everything now.

1. package.json (name alltag, private, type module, packageManager pnpm). deps: react 19, react-dom 19, @google/genai. devDeps: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, tailwindcss v4, @tailwindcss/vite, vitest, jsdom, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, @testing-library/user-event, @vercel/node, @types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, eslint, @eslint/js, typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-react-hooks, globals. scripts: dev "vite", build "vite build", preview "vite preview", test "vitest run", lint "eslint .". Run `pnpm install` and commit pnpm-lock.yaml (node_modules stay ignored).
2. vite.config.ts: react() + tailwindcss() plugins; test: { environment: "jsdom", setupFiles: ["src/test/setup.ts"], include: ["src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}", "api/**/*.test.ts", "docs/**/*.test.ts"], environmentMatchGlobs: [["api/**", "node"], ["docs/**", "node"]] }. src/test/setup.ts imports @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest.
3. ONE tsconfig.json (no project references): strict, noEmit, target ES2022, lib [ES2022, DOM, DOM.Iterable], module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, jsx react-jsx, skipLibCheck, types ["vite/client", "node", "vitest/globals"], include ["src", "api", "docs", "vite.config.ts"]. vitest config globals: true.
4. eslint.config.js flat config: @eslint/js recommended, typescript-eslint recommended, react-hooks recommended-latest, globals browser+node, ignores ["dist", "node_modules"]. `pnpm lint` must pass on the scaffold.
5. vercel.json: {"framework":"vite","functions":{"api/**/*.ts":{"runtime":"@vercel/node@5"}}} or the current documented equivalent; rewrites not needed. api/health.ts: default export handler(req: VercelRequest, res: VercelResponse) -> res.status(200).json({ok:true}). api/health.test.ts starts with `// @vitest-environment node`, calls the handler with a minimal fake req/res (res.status returns res, res.json records the body) and asserts {ok:true}.
6. src/lib/types.ts exact exports: type Level = "A1"|"A2"|"B1"|"B2"; type Gender = "m"|"f"; interface SceneObject {id; fr; en; article; gender: Gender; plural; level: Level; phrase_fr; phrase_en; bbox?: [number,number,number,number] (x,y,w,h as 0..1 fractions)}; interface SceneTask {fr; en; role}; interface SceneResult {place; objects: SceneObject[]; task: SceneTask}; interface SceneRequest {imageBase64; level: Level; knownWords: string[]}; interface TurnMessage {role: "tutor"|"learner"; text}; interface TurnRequest {scene: SceneResult; history: TurnMessage[]; userText; level: Level}; interface TurnResponse {reply_fr; reply_en; task_done: boolean}; type CorrectionType = "article"|"gender"|"case"|"tense"|"word_order"|"vocab"|"register"; interface Correction {said; better; type: CorrectionType; why_en}; interface CorrectRequest {scene: SceneResult; userText; level: Level}; interface CorrectResponse {corrections: Correction[]; kept_phrase_fr}; interface Card {id; phrase_fr; phrase_en; noun_fr?; objectId?; crop?: string (JPEG data URL); place?; errorType?: CorrectionType; ease: number; interval: number (days); reps: number; due: number (epoch ms); learnedAt: number (epoch ms)}; interface GradiumToken {token; expires_at: string}. All unannotated fields are string.
7. src/lib/screen.ts: export type Screen = "look"|"scene"|"roleplay"|"corrections"|"review"|"diary"|"settings"; a module-level store (useSyncExternalStore) so `go(screen)` works outside React; export function useScreen(): {screen: Screen; go: (s: Screen) => void} and export const go. Initial screen "look". src/lib/screen.test.ts: initial is look; go("scene") updates a rendered hook (renderHook + act); go with the same screen is a no-op.
8. src/lib/session.ts: export interface Session {scene: SceneResult|null; frame: string|null; recallCardId: string|null; lastExchange: {transcript: TurnMessage[]; corrections: Correction[]; kept_phrase_fr: string[]}|null}; export const session: Session (mutable singleton) and resetSession(). src/lib/settings.ts: export interface Settings {language: "fr"; level: Level; voiceId: string; speed: number}; defaults {language:"fr", level:"A1", voiceId:"YKeBw3OV1RgpdhLh", speed:1}; getSettings()/setSettings(partial) persisted in localStorage key "alltag.settings". src/lib/api.ts: postScene(req: SceneRequest): Promise<SceneResult>, postTurn(req: TurnRequest): Promise<TurnResponse>, postCorrect(req: CorrectRequest): Promise<CorrectResponse>, getGradiumToken(): Promise<GradiumToken>; each does fetch("/api/<name>") with JSON and throws Error(`<name> ${status}`) on non-2xx.
9. src/styles/tokens.css: CSS custom properties on :root, placeholder values with stable names (the human pastes canvas values later; add that comment): --bg #F6F4EF, --card #FFFFFF, --ink #1B1B1A, --muted #6B6965, --line #E4E1DA, --accent #2F6F5E, --accent-soft #DCEBE4, --warn #B8542F, --due #D9A441, --radius-s 12px, --radius-m 20px, --radius-pill 999px, --font system-ui, -apple-system, "Inter", sans-serif, --text-xs 13px, --text-s 15px, --text-m 17px, --text-l 22px, --text-xl 28px, --space-1..6 = 4,8,12,16,24,32px. src/index.css: @import "tailwindcss"; @import "./styles/tokens.css"; body uses var(--bg), var(--ink), var(--font); @theme maps --color-accent etc. to the vars so Tailwind classes like bg-accent work.
10. index.html (viewport-fit=cover, mobile-first, title "alltag"), src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx: renders the screen from useScreen() via a switch over src/screens/{Look,Scene,Roleplay,Corrections,Review,Diary,Settings}.tsx stubs (each default-exports a component that shows its lowercase name and a button per screen calling go) plus a bottom nav with look / review / diary / settings. Copy lowercase-calm, no emoji.
11. README.md skeleton with the 11 section headings from idea.md section 11 and one sentence each; a "Entire" section stating a human runs `entire enable` (capture step). .env.example with GEMINI_API_KEY=, GRADIUM_API_KEY=, GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash and a comment per var. .gitignore: append node_modules, dist, .env, .env.*.local, .vercel, keep existing lines. public/favicon.svg simple mark.
Keep the gate green: `npm test -- --watch=false`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`.
acceptance: api/health.test.ts passes: handler responds 200 {ok:true} (node environment)
src/lib/screen.test.ts passes: initial screen look, go("scene") re-renders the hook, same-screen go is a no-op
`npm test -- --watch=false`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` all exit 0 at the repo root (.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh green)
src/lib/types.ts exports every name listed in the spec item 6 and src/lib/screen.ts exports Screen, useScreen, go; src/lib/{session,settings,api}.ts export the listed functions
No file outside the scope list is created; pnpm-lock.yaml is committed; .env.example lists GEMINI_API_KEY, GRADIUM_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL

constraints.allowed_dependencies: all packages listed in spec item 1; nothing else
constraints.interface_contract: src/lib/types.ts, screen.ts, session.ts, settings.ts, api.ts shapes are consumed verbatim by tasks B..H; do not rename fields

input.spec:
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first (node_modules are not committed). No new dependencies. Types come from src/lib/types.ts (import with a relative path, e.g. "../src/lib/types"); do not edit it.

api/scene.ts: Vercel Node handler (VercelRequest/VercelResponse, same pattern as api/health.ts). POST body SceneRequest {imageBase64, level, knownWords[]}. 405 on non-POST. 400 {error} when imageBase64 is missing/not a string or level is not A1..B2 (knownWords defaults to []). Strip a leading "data:image/jpeg;base64," prefix if present. Call Gemini with `@google/genai`: `const ai = new GoogleGenAI({apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY})`; `ai.models.generateContent({model: process.env.GEMINI_MODEL ?? input.title: C: Add api/turn.ts and api/correct.ts Gemini dialogue and grader routes
input.spec:
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first. No new dependencies. Types from src/lib/types.ts (relative import, do not edit). Two separate Gemini calls by design (idea.md section 6): the tutor stays in character, the grader grades; neither prompt may be shared or merged.

Common pattern for both routes (duplicate the few lines, do not create a shared module outside scope): Vercel handler, 405 on non-POST, 400 {error} on missing required fields, 500 {error:"missing_key"} without GEMINI_API_KEY, `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey})`, `ai.models.generateContent({model: process.env.GEMINI_MODEL ?? "gemini-2.5-flash", contents:[{role:"user", parts:[{text:user}]}], config:{systemInstruction: system, responseMimeType:"application/json", responseSchema}})`, parse `response.text`, validate by hand, 502 {error} on bad output. Export `createHandler(deps:{generate})` and default-export the real one, like api/scene.ts.

api/turn.ts: POST TurnRequest {scene, history[], userText, level} -> TurnResponse {reply_fr, reply_en, task_done}. api/_prompts/turn.ts exports TURN_SCHEMA and buildTurnPrompt({scene, history, userText, level}): {system, user}. System: you are Noé, a calm barista in Zurich, playing the role scene.task.role in scene.place; speak only French in reply_fr, at most 2 short sentences, level ceiling <level>, use the scene objects by their fr names with articles, introduce at most 2 new words per turn, never correct the learner mid-dialogue, keep the task scene.task.fr moving, set task_done true only when the learner has accomplished the task; reply_en is a plain English gloss. User prompt lists the objects (fr, article, gender), the task, the history as "tutor: ..." / "learner: ..." lines, then the learner's latest line.

api/correct.ts: POST CorrectRequest {scene, userText, level} -> CorrectResponse {corrections[{said, better, type, why_en}], kept_phrase_fr}. api/_prompts/correct.ts exports CORRECT_SCHEMA and buildCorrectPrompt({scene, userText, level}): {system, user}. System: you are a French grader, not a tutor persona; return only real errors in the learner's sentence, each with type from exactly article|gender|case|tense|word_order|vocab|register, why_en one short English sentence, better = the minimal corrected fragment; kept_phrase_fr = the whole learner sentence corrected, natural, worth memorising; empty corrections array when the sentence is fine. Validation drops corrections whose type is outside the enum. Grader prompt must not mention Noé or the barista role.

Tests (`// @vitest-environment node`): api/turn.test.ts: fake generate returns a TurnResponse JSON -> 200 equal; the prompt text contains every scene object fr name and the latest userText and a history line; missing userText -> 400; task_done non-boolean -> 502. api/correct.test.ts: fake returns 2 corrections (one with an invalid type) -> 200 with only the valid one and kept_phrase_fr; missing scene -> 400; the system prompt does not contain "Noé"; the turn system prompt does contain "Noé".
acceptance: api/turn.test.ts passes: 200 TurnResponse from fake generator, prompt contains all scene object names, history and userText, 400 on missing userText, 502 when task_done is not boolean
api/correct.test.ts passes: invalid correction types are dropped, kept_phrase_fr returned, 400 on missing scene, grader system prompt contains no "Noé" while the turn system prompt does
api/_prompts/turn.ts and api/_prompts/correct.ts export their SCHEMA and build*Prompt functions; both routes export createHandler and a default Vercel handler
Gate green: npm test -- --watch=false, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint

input.title: D: Add Gradium token route and browser STT/TTS voice client with useVoice state machine
input.spec:
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first. No new dependencies. Types from src/lib/types.ts; getGradiumToken from src/lib/api.ts; settings from src/lib/settings.ts. Do not edit those. Gradium facts verified from docs.gradium.ai on 2026-10-10 (prefer these over memory):
- Token exchange: GET https://api.gradium.ai/api/api-keys/token with header x-api-key: <GRADIUM_API_KEY> -> {token, expires_at}. Tokens are single-use (consumed on verify): fetch a fresh one for every socket.
- STT: wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr?token=<token>. First message {type:"setup", model_name:"default", input_format:"pcm", json_config:{language:"fr", delay_in_frames:10}}. Audio: 24 kHz 16-bit signed LE mono PCM, 1920 samples (80 ms) per message {type:"audio", audio:<base64>}. Server messages: {type:"text", text, start_s}, {type:"end_text", stop_s}, {type:"step", vad:[{horizon_s:0.5|1|2|3, inactivity_prob}]}, {type:"flushed", flush_id}, {type:"end_of_stream"}. Client {type:"send_flush", flush_id} forces a boundary; {type:"end_of_stream"} closes.
- TTS: wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts?token=<token>. First message {type:"setup", voice_id, model_name:"default", output_format:"pcm"}; then {type:"text", text}; then {type:"end_of_stream"}. Server {type:"audio", audio:<base64 PCM16 48 kHz mono>} chunks, then {type:"end_of_stream"}.

api/gradium-token.ts: Vercel handler, GET or POST, 500 {error:"missing_key"} without GRADIUM_API_KEY, fetches the token URL with x-api-key, returns 200 {token, expires_at} (GradiumToken) and Cache-Control: no-store; upstream non-2xx -> 502 {error:"token_failed"}. Export createHandler({fetchImpl}) for tests. api/gradium-token.test.ts (`// @vitest-environment node`): fake fetch returns {token:"t1", expires_at:"2026-10-10T20:00:00Z"} -> body has token and expires_at and the serialized body does not contain the key value; missing env -> 500; upstream 401 -> 502.

input.spec:
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first. No new dependencies. Consume verbatim and do not edit: src/lib/{types,screen,session,settings}.ts, src/srs/store.ts (all/due/grade/byNoun/remove/clear), src/voice/useVoice.ts (may be absent if task D is not merged yet: import it lazily inside a try, or render a text-input fallback when the hook throws; the Review test mocks it with vi.mock). Boards to match: ReviewQueue (header "due now" with the count, groups by error type with a one-line summary such as "you keep dropping the article on feminine nouns" for article/gender groups, generic "N to say again" otherwise; empty state "nothing due, go look at something"), ReviewCard (the card's crop image or a place line, prompt "say it: " + phrase_en, hold-to-talk control, after the attempt a result line "good, next in N days" or "not yet, again tomorrow" and a "next" button), Diary (grid of kept cards: crop thumbnail, phrase_fr, place, ISO date of learnedAt; header "what you can say now"; empty state), Settings (language fixed to French, level select A1..B2, voice select with the French voices: Jules YKeBw3OV1RgpdhLh, Marius biuhvu17TxVKOcyy, Gaspard iEu63s1rhn_kegTr, Solène YhIHaAfQ0cQPDV9R, Noémie FXxJ9mANRq6BCTX5; speed 0.8..1.2; a data note "everything stays in this browser" and a "clear everything" button calling store.clear() after a confirm()). Copy lowercase-calm, no emoji, token vars.

src/srs/recall.ts: export normalizeNoun(s: string): string (lowercase, trim, strip accents via NFD, drop a leading article le/la/les/l'/un/une/des); export findRecall(scene: SceneResult, cards: Card[], now = Date.now()): Card|null returning the first card (by earliest due) whose noun_fr normalises equal to some scene object fr and whose due <= now; else null. export similarity(a: string, b: string): number in 0..1 (normalised Levenshtein over normalizeNoun-style cleaned strings) and gradeFromTranscript(transcript: string, target: string): 0|1|3|5 (>= 0.85 -> 5, >= 0.6 -> 3, non-empty -> 1, empty -> 0).

Recall hook: edit src/screens/Scene.tsx only at the "talk" handler: before go("roleplay") set session.recallCardId = findRecall(session.scene, store.all())?.id ?? null. Keep every existing test in Look.test.tsx green.

src/screens/Review.tsx (replace the stub): queue = store.due() grouped by errorType ?? "phrase"; tap a group or "start" to open the first due card; hold-to-talk via useVoice(onFinal: transcript -> q = gradeFromTranscript(transcript, card.phrase_fr) -> store.grade(card.id, q) -> result line with the new interval); a text input fallback labelled "or type it" always rendered so the flow works without a mic; "next" advances through the due list and returns to the queue at the end.
src/screens/Diary.tsx (replace the stub): grid of store.all() sorted by learnedAt desc.
src/screens/Settings.tsx (replace the stub): controlled inputs bound to getSettings()/setSettings().

Tests (jsdom): src/srs/recall.test.ts: findRecall returns the due card whose noun matches "la machine à café" vs scene object fr "machine à café" (article and accents ignored), returns null when the card is not due or no noun matches, picks the earliest due of two matches; gradeFromTranscript("je voudrais un café", "je voudrais un café") is 5 and ("un café", "je voudrais un café s'il vous plaît") is below 5. src/screens/Review.test.tsx: vi.mock("../voice/useVoice"); seed two due cards (errorType article and gender) and one future card: the queue shows "2" due and a group for article; start -> card shows "say it" with phrase_en; typing the exact phrase_fr in the fallback input and submitting grades 5 (store.get(id).reps === 1, interval 1) and shows "next in 1 day"; next -> second card; after the last, the queue shows the empty state. src/screens/Diary.test.tsx: three kept cards render three tiles with phrase_fr and an ISO date; empty store renders the empty state.
acceptance: src/srs/recall.test.ts passes: findRecall matches nouns ignoring article and accents, returns null when not due or unmatched, picks the earliest due; gradeFromTranscript grades exact match 5 and a partial below 5
src/screens/Review.test.tsx passes: due count and error-type group, say-it card, typed exact answer grades 5 and shows next-in interval, next advances, empty state after the last card
src/screens/Diary.test.tsx passes: one tile per kept card with phrase_fr and ISO date, empty state when the store is empty
Scene.tsx talk handler sets session.recallCardId via findRecall and src/screens/Look.test.tsx still passes; Settings.tsx persists level/voiceId/speed through setSettings
Gate green: npm test -- --watch=false, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint

input.title: H: Complete README, docs, PWA manifest and ship checks
input.spec:
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first. No new dependencies. Docs task: read the merged code before writing; every path, route, env var and schema you cite must exist in the tree. Half the grade reads the README (idea.md section 11 is the outline; sections 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 of idea.md are the source material, condense them, do not paste them whole).

README.md (replace the skeleton), sections in this order: 1 what it is (one paragraph + the LOOK/LISTEN/DO/FIX/KEEP loop as an ASCII diagram); 2 why (the research table and the competitor gap, short); 3 setup (`pnpm i`, `.env` with GEMINI_API_KEY, GRADIUM_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL from .env.example, `pnpm dev`, `vercel deploy`, Vercel env vars); 4 architecture (ASCII diagram of browser, serverless, Gradium, Gemini; the two-call tutor design and why); 5 API table: one row per route in api/*.ts (exclude _prompts and tests): /api/health, /api/scene, /api/turn, /api/correct, /api/gradium-token with method, request and response fields taken from src/lib/types.ts; 6 partner tech: Gradium (STT/TTS WebSocket, semantic VAD, token exchange) with file paths src/voice/stt.ts, src/voice/tts.ts, api/gradium-token.ts; Gemini (vision, dialogue, grader) with api/scene.ts, api/turn.ts, api/correct.ts, api/_prompts/*; Entire (session capture behind commits) with the enable step and a placeholder link line "checkpoints branch: <the human fills this in>"; 7 latency table with the four hops from idea.md section 6 and empty "measured" cells the human fills at the venue; 8 learning design (level control 95 % rule, correction taxonomy, SM-2 by production, camera-triggered recall) with the file paths src/srs/store.ts and src/srs/recall.ts; 9 Entire: how to browse the build sessions; 10 what we did not build and why (accounts, multiple languages, streaks, phoneme scoring, voice design, S2S translate); 11 team and licence (MIT, team names left as a placeholder line).
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: the dialogue state machine (idle, listening, thinking, speaking, correcting), the session/screen singletons, data that stays in localStorage, the WebSocket message flow with the exact Gradium message shapes used in src/voice. docs/API.md: per route the request and response JSON example and error codes as implemented.
PWA: public/manifest.webmanifest (name alltag, short_name alltag, display standalone, start_url /, theme and background colours from src/styles/tokens.css, icons public/icon-192.svg and public/icon-512.svg as simple SVG marks with type image/svg+xml); link it from index.html with <link rel="manifest"> and a theme-color meta. Verify vercel.json still matches the api/ layout and that `pnpm build` succeeds (run it; do not commit dist).
docs/readme.test.ts (`// @vitest-environment node`): reads README.md, lists api/*.ts excluding *.test.ts and files under _prompts, and asserts the README contains "/api/<basename>" for each; parses .env.example and asserts each VAR name appears in the README; asserts README contains "Entire", "Gradium" and "Gemini"; asserts public/manifest.webmanifest parses as JSON with name "alltag".
acceptance: docs/readme.test.ts passes: README names every /api route found in api/*.ts, every env var in .env.example, the words Entire, Gradium and Gemini; manifest parses with name alltag
README.md has the 11 sections in the order of the spec, an API table with the five routes and an ASCII architecture diagram; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/API.md exist with the content described
`pnpm build` exits 0 and index.html links public/manifest.webmanifest
Gate green: npm test -- --watch=false, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint

content.content:
T-0002 is done and committed on `task/T-0002` in two commits: `3814b37` (scaffold) and `d1a3fe5` (removes a file that slipped into the first one). The gate (`.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh .`) passes: 4 tests, tsc and lint all exit 0. `vite build` also succeeds.

## Summary
The app scaffold matches spec items 1 to 11. `types.ts`, `screen.ts`, `session.ts`, `settings.ts` and `api.ts` have the exact names and field shapes from the spec. The screen store uses `useSyncExternalStore`, so `go()` works outside React, and calling `go` with the current screen does nothing.

Where I departed from the spec, and why:
- **TypeScript is pinned to `~6.0`.** The latest is 7.0.2, but typescript-eslint 8 only supports TypeScript below 6.1, so 7 failed its peer dependency check.
- **No `environmentMatchGlobs` in `vite.config.ts`.** vitest 5 removed that option. I used `test.projects` to get the same split: `src` tests run in jsdom, `api` and `docs` tests run in node. `api/health.test.ts` also has the `// @vitest-environment node` line.
- **No `runtime` entry in `vercel.json`.** Vercel already runs `api/*.ts` as Node functions, and `runtime` is only for community runtimes. I used `functions: {"api/**/*.ts": {"maxDuration": 30}}` instead.
- **No radius mapping in `@theme`.** Tailwind's radius theme variables have the same names as our `--radius-*` tokens, so mapping them would make each variable refer to itself. Colors and font are mapped, so classes like `bg-accent` work.

## Still open: `pnpm install` exits with code 1
pnpm 11 refuses to finish because `@google/genai`, `esbuild` and `protobufjs` want to run build scripts that haven't been approved. To record the approvals, pnpm generated a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with an `allowBuilds` block. That file is outside this task's write scope, so I removed it in the second commit. Approving the scripts in `package.json` instead had no effect in pnpm 11.

The gate is unaffected because it runs through npm and npx. But anyone running `pnpm i` as the README says will hit the error. The fix is a follow-up task that adds `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `allowBuilds: { esbuild: true, "@google/genai": false, protobufjs: false }`.

No dependencies were added beyond the list in spec item 1. I committed because the task told me to, even though your house rules normally ask for approval first. Nothing was pushed.

## Files changed
`package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `vercel.json`, `index.html`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `public/favicon.svg`, `api/health.ts`, `api/health.test.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/index.css`, `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/test/setup.ts`, `src/lib/{types,screen,screen.test,session,settings,api}.ts`, `src/screens/{Look,Scene,Roleplay,Corrections,Review,Diary,Settings}.tsx`

None.

# Alltag design language (v1, 2026-10-10)

Alltag teaches a language from the room you are in: camera on an object,
a tutor voice names it, you get through a small spoken interaction, you
get corrected after, the fumbles come back later. No courses, no streaks.

## Two surfaces
- **Camera surfaces** (viewfinder, scene labels, roleplay over the live image,
  recall trigger): near-black ground, white type, glass pills. Content is the
  user's own world; chrome stays out of the way.
- **Learning surfaces** (object sheet, corrections, review, diary, settings,
  onboarding): light paper ground, ink type, one accent.

## Colors (CSS tokens; write them INLINE, not as CSS vars, except in helmet)
Ground
- paper      #F6F5F2   light ground
- card       #FFFFFF   cards on paper
- line       #E3E1DB   hairlines on paper
- ink        #15181C   primary text on paper
- ink2       #5B6069   secondary text on paper (4.5:1 on paper)
- night      #0D0F12   camera ground
- glass      rgba(20,22,26,0.62) pills over camera, blur 18px, 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.14) border
- snow       #FFFFFF   text on camera

Accent
- moss       #0F6E56   the one accent. Buttons, active state, "better" text
- mossSoft   #DDEFE7   accent tint for chips / selected rows
- clay       #B84A1C   "what you said" in corrections, errors (3.9:1 on paper at 24px+, use 20px+ or bold)
- claySoft   #F7E3DA   tint behind clay text
- sun        #F2C94C   recall / "we saw this before" highlight, only on camera surfaces

Semantic
- success = moss, attention = clay, memory = sun. Never red/green together.

## Type (Google Fonts, both in <helmet>)
- Display: "Bricolage Grotesque", weights 500/700. Headlines, target-language words, labels on camera.
- Body: "Instrument Sans", 400/500/600. Everything else.
Helmet link:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bricolage+Grotesque:opsz,wght@12..96,500;12..96,700&family=Instrument+Sans:wght@400;500;600&display=swap">

Scale (px / line-height)
- hero 44/48 display 700 (target word on object sheet, onboarding titles)
- h1 32/38 display 700
- h2 24/30 display 500
- title 18/24 body 600
- body 16/24 body 400
- small 14/20 body 500
- micro 12/16 body 500, letter-spacing 0.04em, uppercase for eyebrows

Target-language text is ALWAYS display face. Native-language gloss is body face in ink2.

## Spacing and shape
- 8px grid. Screen side gutter 20px. Section gap 24px. Card padding 16px.
- Radii: card 20px, pill 999px, sheet top 28px, chip 10px, button 16px.
- Buttons: primary moss bg, snow text, 56px tall, body 600 17px. Secondary: card bg, ink text, 1px line.
- Touch targets ≥ 44px.
- Shadows: none on paper. Camera pills use glass only.

## Phone frame
- 390×844. No fake status bar. Home indicator: none. Top safe inset 54px, bottom 34px (leave as padding).
- Bottom nav on learning surfaces only, 3 items: Look (camera), Review, Diary. Icons inline stroke SVG 24px, label micro. Active = moss.
- Camera surfaces have no bottom nav: a single shutter / mic control row.

## Components (draw these consistently)
- **Viewfinder brackets**: four 28px L corners, 3px snow, radius 6, 24px in from the photo edge. (ref: CapWords)
- **Scene label**: glass pill, display 16px snow target word, then body 13px rgba(255,255,255,0.72) gloss. Small 6px moss dot on the left when the word is already known, sun dot when a card is due. Anchored to a 8px leader dot on the object.
- **Task pill**: top center on roleplay, glass, micro eyebrow "YOUR TASK" + body 15px snow. (ref: Speak)
- **Tutor bubble**: glass card max-width 320px, display 18px snow for the target language line, body 14px gloss below, 3 icon buttons: replay, translate, slower.
- **Mic control**: 72px circle. Idle: card bg, moss mic icon. Listening: moss bg, snow bars waveform. Thinking: glass, three dots. Speaking (tutor): glass with a moss ring. Label under it in micro: "Hold to talk" / "Listening" / "Thinking" / "Tap to interrupt".
- **Correction card** (ref: Speak, Duolingo): card, eyebrow micro ink2 with error type chip (GENDER, ARTICLE, TENSE, WORD ORDER, VOCAB, REGISTER). Line 1 "You said" small ink2, then display 18px clay with the wrong token underlined. Line 2 "Better" small ink2, display 18px moss. Then body 15px ink2 why, max 2 lines. Footer: "Say it again" secondary button + bookmark icon.
- **Review card**: card with photo crop on top (aspect 4:3, radius 20px top), below: micro eyebrow of the place ("YOUR KITCHEN · 2 DAYS AGO"), body 16px task ("Ask where this is"). Mic control centered under. (ref: CapWords hold-to-speak, Babbel "did you remember")
- **Error type group header** on review queue: display 20px ink "Feminine articles", small ink2 "4 due · you drop *la* before nouns you just learned".
- **Diary tile**: photo 1:1 radius 16, on-image bottom gradient, display 15px snow phrase, micro gloss date.
- **Level meter**: thin 4px moss bar, label "A1 → A2" micro.
- **Photo placeholders**: never a grey box with "image". Use a soft two-tone CSS gradient block (e.g. linear-gradient(160deg,#3A3F47,#1C1F24)) with a small inline SVG outline of the object (cup, machine, ticket) centered at 30% opacity, and a micro caption "[PHOTO: coffee machine]" bottom-left in gloss. On paper surfaces use #E9E7E1 → #D6D3CB.

## Copy
Target language for the demo: French. Native: English. Tutor name: "Noé". Persona: Zurich café barista, warm, short sentences.
Microcopy is lowercase-calm, no exclamation marks, no emoji. "Point at anything." "Hold to talk." "Say it again." "We saw this before."

## Don'ts
- No streaks, XP, flames, gems, leaderboards, mascots.
- No gradient washes on paper, no left-border cards, no emoji icons.
- No Inter/Roboto/Arial.
- No fake status bars.
---
# Alltag boards — what is on each screen

Demo scenario used across ALL boards (keep it consistent):
- Learner: English speaker, French A1, in Zurich. Tutor: Noé, café barista persona.
- Scene 1: a café counter at the hackathon venue. Objects: la machine à café, une tasse, le lait, un croissant, la carte (menu), la caisse.
- Task: "Order a coffee with milk and ask how much it is."
- Learner said: "Je veux le café avec le lait." → better: "Je voudrais un café au lait, s'il vous plaît." (register + article). Also said "le machine" → "la machine" (gender).
- Second scene for recall: same machine two days later.
- Review queue groups: "Feminine articles" (4 due), "Politeness: je voudrais" (2 due), "Food words" (3 due).
- Diary entries: "la machine à café" (café, today), "un billet, s'il vous plaît" (Hauptbahnhof, yesterday), "où est le lait ?" (kitchen, 3 days ago), "une table pour deux" (restaurant, last week).

Sheet boards are 1200 wide. Phone boards 390×844. Night = camera surface, Paper = learning surface.

## Foundations.dc.html (1200×1320, paper)
Title "Foundations". Four sections in a 12-col feel:
1. Color: swatch tiles for paper, card, line, ink, ink2, night, glass, moss, mossSoft, clay, claySoft, sun. Each tile: 96×72 block, name, hex, role line.
2. Type: live specimens of hero 44, h1 32, h2 24, title 18, body 16, small 14, micro 12, each with the French sample "la machine à café" in display and the English gloss in body.
3. Spacing and shape: 8px grid row of blocks (4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48), radii samples (chip 10, button 16, card 20, sheet 28, pill 999).
4. Surfaces: two mini cards side by side, "Camera surfaces: night ground, glass pills, snow text, sun for memory" and "Learning surfaces: paper, cards, moss accent, clay for what you said". Rule list under it: no streaks, no XP, no mascots, no emoji, correction after the turn.

## Research.dc.html (1200×1320, paper)
Title "Research · what we took from Mobbin and why". A grid of 12 reference rows (3 columns × 4). Each: app name (display 18), what we took (body 14), link as `<a href>` to the mobbin_url, and a tag chip of which board uses it. Entries:
- CapWords camera: bracket corners, "Curious how to say this in French? Tap to snap", soft shutter. → CameraIdle. https://mobbin.com/screens/a56da769-84dd-4cc0-892c-027cf372698f
- Lifesum "Snap a meal": full-bleed photo, bottom dark sheet with eyebrow + headline + shutter. → CameraScanning. https://mobbin.com/screens/1aeee107-a9ef-4770-91a4-827bb3c62ffd
- Speak roleplay: task pill top, tutor line in glass bubble with replay/translate, "Tap to respond" mic. → RoleplayStart. https://mobbin.com/screens/55235d18-59b0-4708-b3dc-77d37a7fbea4
- Tolan: camera + chat + mic as one control row under a character. → control row. https://mobbin.com/screens/e3d06f86-9c1d-466e-aeb0-342a2e6ed946
- Claude voice: single wide pill with waveform, settings left, close right. → RoleplayListening. https://mobbin.com/screens/13cf4949-114a-4686-a9ef-9c80f694c801
- Pi "is listening": calm, text only state. → thinking state copy. https://mobbin.com/screens/7f86354d-c06a-4c2f-8396-616c1ac2995c
- Speak correction cards: orange "what you said" / green "better" / why / Retry. → Corrections. https://mobbin.com/screens/c7abdc8b-c155-424c-b22c-ac79535784e0
- Duolingo correction explanation: strike + replacement, examples list. → Corrections why. https://mobbin.com/screens/26c5c998-56b0-410b-9f81-326fdb66dcaa

- **Viewfinder brackets**: four 28px L corners, 3px snow, radius 6, 24px in from the photo edge. (ref: CapWords)
- **Scene label**: glass pill, display 16px snow target word, then body 13px rgba(255,255,255,0.72) gloss. Small 6px moss dot on the left when the word is already known, sun dot when a card is due. Anchored to a 8px leader dot on the object.
- **Task pill**: top center on roleplay, glass, micro eyebrow "YOUR TASK" + body 15px snow. (ref: Speak)
- **Tutor bubble**: glass card max-width 320px, display 18px snow for the target language line, body 14px gloss below, 3 icon buttons: replay, translate, slower.
- **Mic control**: 72px circle. Idle: card bg, moss mic icon. Listening: moss bg, snow bars waveform. Thinking: glass, three dots. Speaking (tutor): glass with a moss ring. Label under it in micro: "Hold to talk" / "Listening" / "Thinking" / "Tap to interrupt".
- **Correction card** (ref: Speak, Duolingo): card, eyebrow micro ink2 with error type chip (GENDER, ARTICLE, TENSE, WORD ORDER, VOCAB, REGISTER). Line 1 "You said" small ink2, then display 18px clay with the wrong token underlined. Line 2 "Better" small ink2, display 18px moss. Then body 15px ink2 why, max 2 lines. Footer: "Say it again" secondary button + bookmark icon.
- **Review card**: card with photo crop on top (aspect 4:3, radius 20px top), below: micro eyebrow of the place ("YOUR KITCHEN · 2 DAYS AGO"), body 16px task ("Ask where this is"). Mic control centered under. (ref: CapWords hold-to-speak, Babbel "did you remember")
- **Error type group header** on review queue: display 20px ink "Feminine articles", small ink2 "4 due · you drop *la* before nouns you just learned".
- **Diary tile**: photo 1:1 radius 16, on-image bottom gradient, display 15px snow phrase, micro gloss date.
- **Level meter**: thin 4px moss bar, label "A1 → A2" micro.

Use a soft two-tone CSS gradient block (e.g. linear-gradient(160deg,#3A3F47,#1C1F24)) with a small inline SVG outline of the object (cup, machine, ticket) centered at 30% opacity, and a micro caption "[PHOTO: coffee machine]" bottom-left in gloss. On paper surfaces use #E9E7E1 → #D6D3CB.

Target language for the demo: French. Native: English. Tutor name: "Noé". Persona: Zurich café barista, warm, short sentences.
Microcopy is lowercase-calm, no exclamation marks, no emoji. "Point at anything." "Hold to talk." "Say it again." "We saw this before."

- No streaks, XP, flames, gems, leaderboards, mascots.
- No gradient washes on paper, no left-border cards, no emoji icons.
- No Inter/Roboto/Arial.

input.title: A2: Approve pnpm build scripts and write design tokens from STYLE.md
input.spec:
Two small fixes after the scaffold (T-0002). No new dependencies. Note: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` currently exits 1 with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS but node_modules is complete and the gate passes; run it once anyway, ignore the exit code, then do the work.

1. pnpm 11 refuses to finish install until build scripts are approved. Add pnpm-workspace.yaml at the repo root containing exactly the allowBuilds block pnpm expects: `allowBuilds:` with `esbuild: true`, `"@google/genai": false`, `protobufjs: false` (and `packages: ["."]` only if pnpm requires a packages key; verify by running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` afterwards: it must exit 0 and must not modify pnpm-lock.yaml; if the lockfile changes, run `pnpm install` and commit the updated lockfile instead, saying so in the summary).

2. Replace src/styles/tokens.css with the real design language from .orchestrator/design/STYLE.md (read it fully). Define on :root the STYLE.md names as CSS custom properties: --paper #F6F5F2, --card #FFFFFF, --line #E3E1DB, --ink #15181C, --ink2 #5B6069, --night #0D0F12, --glass rgba(20,22,26,0.62), --glass-border rgba(255,255,255,0.14), --snow #FFFFFF, --moss #0F6E56, --moss-soft #DDEFE7, --clay #B84A1C, --clay-soft #F7E3DA, --sun #F2C94C; fonts --font-display "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif and --font-body "Instrument Sans", sans-serif; type scale --text-hero 44px/48px, --text-h1 32px/38px, --text-h2 24px/30px, --text-title 18px/24px, --text-body 16px/24px, --text-small 14px/20px, --text-micro 12px/16px (define size and line-height as separate vars, e.g. --text-h1 and --lh-h1); radii --radius-chip 10px, --radius-button 16px, --radius-card 20px, --radius-sheet 28px, --radius-pill 999px; --gutter 20px; --safe-top 54px; --safe-bottom 34px. KEEP every existing token name from the current file as an alias so nothing in flight breaks: --bg: var(--paper); --muted: var(--ink2); --accent: var(--moss); --accent-soft: var(--moss-soft); --warn: var(--clay); --due: var(--sun); --radius-s: var(--radius-chip); --radius-m: var(--radius-card); --font: var(--font-body); --text-xs..--text-xl and --space-1..6 unchanged. Update the @theme block in src/index.css so Tailwind classes exist for the new names (--color-paper, --color-ink, --color-ink2, --color-night, --color-snow, --color-moss, --color-moss-soft, --color-clay, --color-clay-soft, --color-sun, --color-line, --color-card, --font-display, --font-body) while keeping the existing mappings; body uses var(--paper), var(--ink), var(--font-body); headings and .display use var(--font-display). Add the Google Fonts stylesheet link from STYLE.md (Bricolage Grotesque 500/700 and Instrument Sans 400/500/600, display=swap) plus preconnect links to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com in index.html <head>.

No test file is required beyond keeping the gate green; do not change any component.
acceptance: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0 at the repo root (approved builds recorded in pnpm-workspace.yaml) and pnpm-lock.yaml is unchanged or its update is committed and explained
src/styles/tokens.css defines every STYLE.md token listed in the spec and keeps every previous token name as an alias (grep finds --bg, --accent, --due, --font, --radius-m, --space-6)
index.html head contains the Google Fonts link for Bricolage Grotesque and Instrument Sans with preconnect links
Gate green: npm test -- --watch=false, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint

## AMENDMENT 11:40 (human): latest Gemini models, Gemini Live for the live roleplay
Verified on ai.google.dev 2026-10-10. Model per job (env-overridable, these are the defaults):
- GEMINI_MODEL_VISION = gemini-3.8-flash (stable): scene parsing (api/scene), structured JSON.
- GEMINI_MODEL_GRADER = gemini-3.8-flash: corrections (api/correct) and turn fallback (api/turn), structured JSON.
- GEMINI_MODEL_LIVE = gemini-3.8-live (stable Live API, native audio in/out, barge-in): the roleplay conversation itself, replacing the Gradium STT -> api/turn -> Gradium TTS loop for the roleplay ONLY. gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking exists but adds delay: do not use.
- Drop gemini-2.5-flash everywhere. Keep GEMINI_MODEL as a legacy alias of GEMINI_MODEL_GRADER if already referenced.

Gemini Live facts (official docs): browser connects with an EPHEMERAL TOKEN, never the key. Server: `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey}).authTokens.create({config:{uses:1, expireTime:<now+30min>, newSessionExpireTime:<now+1min>, liveConnectConstraints:{model:"gemini-3.8-live", ...}}})` -> token.name; browser: `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey: token.name, httpOptions:{apiVersion:"v1beta"}})` then `ai.live.connect({model, config:{responseModalities:["AUDIO"], speechConfig:{voiceConfig:{prebuiltVoiceConfig:{voiceName:"Puck"}}}, systemInstruction, inputAudioTranscription:{}, outputAudioTranscription:{}, tools:[{functionDeclarations:[{name:"mark_task_done", description:"call when the learner completed the task", parameters:{type:"OBJECT",properties:{}}}]}]}, callbacks:{onmessage,onerror,onclose}})`. Audio in: raw PCM16 16 kHz little-endian mono via `session.sendRealtimeInput({audio:{data:<base64>, mimeType:"audio/pcm;rate=16000"}})`; audio out: PCM16 24 kHz in `serverContent.modelTurn.parts[].inlineData`; `serverContent.interrupted` means the user barged in (stop playback, clear the queue); transcripts arrive as `serverContent.inputTranscription.text` / `outputTranscription.text`; turn end `serverContent.turnComplete`. Ephemeral tokens work only with the Live API and v1beta.

What changes in the build order:
- NEW task D2 (deps A; parallel with D, E): `api/live-token.ts` (POST -> {token, expires_at}; mints an ephemeral token constrained to GEMINI_MODEL_LIVE; never returns the key) and `src/voice/live.ts` (`LiveSession`: connect(token, {scene, level, knownWords, task}) builds the system prompt (Noé, barista persona, stays in character, 95 % known words, 1 to 2 new items per turn, never corrects mid-conversation, calls mark_task_done), mic -> 16 kHz PCM16 worklet (reuse D's resampler with a target-rate parameter) -> sendRealtimeInput, output PCM 24 kHz -> AudioContext queue with `stop()` on `interrupted`, emits events: userText(partial/final), tutorText, speaking(bool), taskDone, error; `useLive()` state idle|connecting|listening|speaking|done). Tests with a fake `live.connect` that replays recorded server messages: `src/voice/live.test.ts` (token never contains the key, interrupted clears the queue, transcripts accumulate, mark_task_done -> taskDone), `api/live-token.test.ts`.
- Task F (Roleplay) now depends on D2 and E (not D): the roleplay screen drives `useLive()`; the mic control states map to Live states (listening = Live session open and user speaking per input transcription activity; speaking = output audio playing; tap to interrupt = user just talks, barge-in is native). After taskDone or 4 learner turns: close the session and POST the accumulated transcript to api/correct (grader model) -> Corrections screen as before. api/turn stays as the text fallback when the Live connection fails (StateSlow board) and for tests.
- Task D (Gradium) keeps its scope but its consumers change: Gradium STT = review cards (hold to talk -> transcript -> grade) and the "Not sure, let Noé find out" level check; Gradium TTS (voice Jules) = phrase playback on object sheet, exchange done and diary, and the VoiceIntro screen (names the objects before the Live session opens); Gradium S2S = the Translate button. Document this split in README: "Noé live = Gemini Live, native speaker playback and review = Gradium".
- Task H README: model table with the three Gemini models and why each; Live token flow diagram; partner section updated.
If the SDK field names differ from the above at build time, follow the installed `@google/genai` typings and record the delta in plan-T-0001.md.

## AMENDMENT 11:45 (human): one right model per job, for every job (Live above was the example)
Env names and defaults; every API route reads its own env, no shared GEMINI_MODEL:
| Job | Where | Model | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scene parsing: photo -> objects, articles, levels, task | api/scene | GEMINI_MODEL_VISION = gemini-3.8-flash | one call per scene on the camera path; needs vision + JSON; flash keeps the "point and it answers" feel under 3 s |
| Live roleplay: talk with Noé | src/voice/live.ts via api/live-token | GEMINI_MODEL_LIVE = gemini-3.8-live | native audio, barge-in, lowest turn latency; extended-thinking variant adds delay, not used |
| Corrections after the exchange | api/correct | GEMINI_MODEL_GRADER = gemini-3.1-pro-preview, fallback gemini-3.8-flash after 8 s or on error | runs once per exchange on a transition screen, so quality beats speed; gender/register/word-order judgements are where Pro helps the learner |
| Text roleplay fallback when Live fails | api/turn | GEMINI_MODEL_TURN = gemini-3.8-flash | latency-bound |
| Review answer check: transcript vs target, lenient rubric, SM-2 grade 0..5 | api/check (new, small) | GEMINI_MODEL_CHECK = gemini-3.5-flash-lite | trivial comparison, many calls, must feel instant |
| Level estimate ("Not sure, let Noé find out"; rolling CEFR from transcripts) | api/level (new, small, G or H) | GEMINI_MODEL_LEVEL = gemini-3.8-flash | classification with JSON, moderate volume |
| Tutor intro voice (VoiceIntro), phrase playback (object sheet, exchange done, diary, review) | src/voice/tts.ts | Gradium TTS, voice Jules (YKeBw3OV1RgpdhLh) | native French speaker quality, streamed, cheap, partner tech |
| Review hold-to-talk transcript | src/voice/stt.ts | Gradium STT fr, semantic VAD | accurate French STT with turn detection |
| Translate button | Gradium speech-to-speech | partner tech, one socket, no LLM hop |
| Scene memory / recall / diary | local | none | no model needed |
Rules: never a Pro model on the camera or live path; never a Lite model where a judgement about the learner's language is made; every model id is an env default, documented in README's model table with this "why" column. Task B updates api/scene to GEMINI_MODEL_VISION; C to GEMINI_MODEL_GRADER (+fallback) and GEMINI_MODEL_TURN; G adds api/check; H documents the table. If B or C already merged with gemini-2.5-flash, file a small follow-up task "models: per-job env defaults" (deps B, C) rather than reopening them.
